# Address verdicts both language implementations must agree on.
#
# The guard is enforced in Go (the MCP tool boundary) and in Python (the
# worker, because a job row is not proof of validation). Two implementations
# of one rule drift, and a drift here means one process fetches what the other
# refuses -- so both test suites read this file and must produce the same
# verdict for every line.
#
# Format: <address> <allow|block> <why>

# -- ordinary public addresses --------------------------------------------
8.8.8.8                 allow  public v4
1.1.1.1                 allow  public v4
93.184.216.34           allow  public v4
2606:4700:4700::1111    allow  public v6
2a00:1450:4001:81a::200e allow  public v6

# -- loopback --------------------------------------------------------------
127.0.0.1               block  loopback
127.1.2.3               block  loopback is the whole /8
0.0.0.0                 block  unspecified
::1                     block  loopback v6
::                      block  unspecified v6

# -- RFC1918 and IPv6 unique-local -----------------------------------------
10.0.0.1                block  private
10.255.255.255          block  private
172.16.0.1              block  private
172.31.255.254          block  private
192.168.1.1             block  private
fd00::1                 block  unique-local v6
fc00::1                 block  unique-local v6

# 172.32/12 is outside RFC1918 and must stay reachable.
172.32.0.1              allow  just past the private range
172.15.255.255          allow  just before the private range

# -- link-local ------------------------------------------------------------
169.254.169.254         block  cloud metadata service
169.254.0.1             block  link-local
fe80::1                 block  link-local v6

# -- carrier-grade NAT, where tailnets live --------------------------------
100.64.0.1              block  CGNAT
100.100.100.100         block  CGNAT
100.127.255.255         block  CGNAT
100.63.255.255          allow  just before CGNAT
100.128.0.1             allow  just past CGNAT

# -- IPv4-mapped IPv6: an IPv4 address wearing a hat -----------------------
::ffff:127.0.0.1        block  mapped loopback
::ffff:10.0.0.1         block  mapped private
::ffff:169.254.169.254  block  mapped metadata service
::ffff:8.8.8.8          allow  mapped public

# -- tunnels and translations that reach IPv4 space ------------------------
64:ff9b::7f00:1         block  NAT64
64:ff9b:1::1            block  NAT64 local-use
2002:7f00:1::1          block  6to4 encodes an IPv4 address
2001::1                 block  Teredo

# -- IPv6 outside global unicast -------------------------------------------
# Only 2000::/3 carries allocated routable addresses. Everything else is
# special-purpose or unallocated, and the two languages' "reserved" predicates
# disagree about it, so the rule is an allow-list rather than an enumeration.
100::1                  block  discard-only
4000::1                 block  unallocated
6000::1                 block  unallocated
8000::1                 block  unallocated
c000::1                 block  unallocated
fec0::1                 block  deprecated site-local
0100::1                 block  outside global unicast
1fff::1                 block  just before global unicast
2000::1                 allow  first global unicast address
3fff:ffff::1            allow  last global unicast address

# -- reserved, documentation, benchmarking ---------------------------------
192.0.0.1               block  IETF protocol assignments
192.0.2.1               block  TEST-NET-1
198.51.100.1            block  TEST-NET-2
203.0.113.1             block  TEST-NET-3
198.18.0.1              block  benchmarking
192.88.99.1             block  6to4 relay anycast
240.0.0.1               block  reserved
255.255.255.255         block  broadcast
2001:db8::1             block  documentation

# -- multicast -------------------------------------------------------------
224.0.0.1               block  multicast
239.255.255.250         block  SSDP multicast
ff02::1                 block  link-local multicast v6
ff01::1                 block  interface-local multicast v6
